title: Render to intermediary representation, render from intermediary representation
Rerenders may not be byte stable
description:
## Summary  
Rendering an unchanged PlotComposition at a fixed size, twice in a row, with a freshly constructed VelloRenderer each time, produces **two different images**, chosen nondeterministically. One pixel differs, by one unit, in its green and blue channels.  
The recorded draw-call stream is byte-identical across runs, so the scene being submitted is deterministic — only its rasterisation is not.  
## Reproducer  
examples/aa_nondeterminism.rs:  
  
```
cargo run --example aa_nondeterminism
cargo run --release --example aa_nondeterminism
```
Output on macOS 26.6.1 / Metal:  
  
```
2 distinct outputs over 60 renders of the same scene at 1200x500 (counts 38/22)
  pixel (404, 77) channel 1: 219 vs 218
  pixel (404, 77) channel 2: 219 vs 218
```
Both outcomes recur across runs and across debug/release, at roughly an even split. The affected pixel and values are stable — always (404, 77), always 219 vs 218.  
## What has been ruled out  
* **Not the scene.** Teeing a single render pass into a RecordingScene alongside the Vello scene yields a byte-identical op stream every time (~97 kB of Debug output, compared in full). The draw calls are deterministic.  
* **Not renderer reuse.** Each render constructs its own VelloRenderer, so no backend state carries between renders.  
* **Not accumulating float error.** Exactly two outcomes, never three, over 60+ renders.  
* **Not the plot layer's caches.** Two back-to-back renders with no mutation in between already disagree.  
* **Not --release versus debug.** Both show it at a similar rate.  
## What the trigger looks like  
The differing pixel has R unchanged and G/B one lower, i.e. slightly more coverage of the red mark colour rgb8(200, 30, 30) over the light grey panel background: it is the **antialiased edge of a filled circle**.  
Two elements are each necessary, and neither is interesting on its own: removing the composition-level caption makes it deterministic; removing the point geoms makes it deterministic.  
The caption is nowhere near the differing pixel — it sits in the bottom band, the pixel is at y=77. It only shifts the layout enough to move a mark's edge onto a subpixel position that triggers the bug. So the real trigger appears to be a **specific edge geometry**, not any of these features. Hand-placed circles through the low-level SceneBuilder API (varying count and fractional offsets) did not reproduce it, consistent with it needing one precise subpixel configuration.  
## Impact  
Small but awkward: it makes pixel-exact render tests unreliable. It surfaced while building a round-trip test for plot documents, where an original and a reloaded composition must render identically — that test now carries a tolerance of ≤8 subpixel bytes at ≤1 delta purely because of this, which is a hole a real regression could hide in.  
## Environment  

|                             |                                           |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| OS                          | macOS 26.6.1 (build 25G76), Apple Silicon |
| Backend                     | Metal via wgpu                            |
| rustc                       | 1.95.0 (59807616e 2026-04-14)             |
| vello                       | 0.10.0                                    |
| wgpu / wgpu-hal / wgpu-core | 29.0.3                                    |
| kurbo                       | 0.13.1                                    |
| peniko                      | 0.6.1                                     |
  
Not yet checked on another GPU backend. If it is Metal-specific, or reproduces against Vello directly, this may belong upstream rather than here.
